presentingComplaint: Recurrent lower abdominal cramping with altered bowel habit for over a year, relieved by defecation
history: 18-month history of intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain, typically relieved after passing stool. Bowel habit alternates between loose stools (often first thing in the morning or around stressful periods) and episodes of harder, less frequent stools. Reports bloating and abdominal distension that worsen through the day and improve overnight. Symptoms flare with stress and around examinations at work. No nocturnal symptoms waking her from sleep. No rectal bleeding, no unintentional weight loss, no fever. Diet includes significant caffeine and irregular meals. PMH: migraine, prior investigation for dyspepsia (normal). No family history of colorectal cancer, coeliac disease or inflammatory bowel disease. No recent travel or antibiotic use.
examination: Comfortable, well-nourished, afebrile. Abdomen soft with mild, non-localised lower abdominal tenderness and palpable but non-tender sigmoid colon; no guarding, no rebound, no mass, no organomegaly. No abdominal distension of concern; normal bowel sounds. Digital rectal examination normal with no blood and no mass. Pertinent negatives: no pallor, no lymphadenopathy, no clubbing, no perianal disease, no aphthous ulcers, no joint swelling.
imaging: Not indicated for classic presentation without alarm features; no cross-sectional or endoscopic imaging warranted at this stage
microbiology: n/a - stool studies not routinely required; no infective or travel history
differentialDiagnoses: Colorectal neoplasia (excluded by absence of alarm features and normal age-appropriate risk)
citations: BSG Guidelines on the Management of Irritable Bowel Syndrome 2021
contraindications: Avoid empiric antibiotics - no infective process; rifaximin only if IBS-D confirmed and refractory, not first-line here
Caution with opioid antidiarrhoeals if constipation-predominant phases dominate
Antispasmodics (e.g., hyoscine) contraindicated in glaucoma / significant bladder outflow obstruction
edgeCases: New-onset IBS-like symptoms after age 50, nocturnal symptoms, weight loss, rectal bleeding, anaemia or raised calprotectin are ALARM features mandating colonoscopy - not IBS
Post-infectious IBS can follow gastroenteritis and mimic this picture
Coeliac disease and microscopic colitis are classic mimics that must be excluded with serology/calprotectin before labelling as IBS
expectedMaiK: Classic positive-diagnosis IBS in a young woman meeting Rome IV criteria (recurrent pain related to defecation with change in stool form/frequency) and with no alarm features and normal calprotectin/coeliac screen. This is a clinical diagnosis; extensive or repeated investigation is not warranted and no antibiotics are indicated.
expectedNextQuestions: Are there any alarm features - rectal bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms, or family history of bowel cancer/IBD?
What is the relationship of pain to defecation and how does stool form vary (to apply Rome IV criteria)?
expectedInvestigations: Full blood count, CRP and faecal calprotectin to exclude IBD
Coeliac serology (anti-tTG IgA with total IgA)
regressionAssertions: stewardship tier must be null (non-infective - no empiric antibiotics)
must not flag alarm features (afebrile, no weight loss, normal calprotectin)
